from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.wait(2)
        
        # Highlight components
        box = SurroundingRectangle(equation, color=YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(box))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        lecture_lines = [
            'The complex plane maps numbers in two dimensions.',
            'Real numbers go horizontal; imaginary numbers go vertical.',
            'Every point has a distance and a rotation angle.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite 2: The Complex Plane", lecture_lines)

        # Colors for highlighting
        color_1 = "#58C4DD" # Sky Blue
        color_2 = "#FFFF00" # Yellow
        color_3 = "#FF8080" # Light Coral

        # Create Coordinate System Elements
        # Using simple lines and arrows instead of full Axes for finer grid control
        x_axis = Arrow(start=self.grid['D1'] + LEFT*0.5, end=self.grid['D6'] + RIGHT*0.5, color=WHITE, buff=0)
        y_axis = Arrow(start=self.grid['F3'] + DOWN*0.5, end=self.grid['A3'] + UP*0.5, color=YELLOW, buff=0)
        
        # Fixed FileNotFoundError: replaced MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        re_label = Text("Real", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(re_label, "D6")
        re_label.shift(DOWN * 0.3)
        
        im_label = Text("Imaginary", color=YELLOW, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(im_label, "A3")
        im_label.shift(RIGHT * 0.8)

        origin_point = self.grid['D3']
        point_coords = self.grid['C5'] # Corresponds to 2 units right, 1 unit up from D3
        
        point_dot = Dot(point_coords, color=color_3)
        point_label = Text("2 + i", color=color_3, font_size=24)
        point_label.next_to(point_dot, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        vector_line = Line(origin_point, point_coords, color=color_3, stroke_width=2)
        
        # Angle and Radius labels
        radius_label = Text("r", color=color_3, font_size=24)
        radius_label.move_to(vector_line.get_center() + UP * 0.2 + LEFT * 0.2)
        
        angle_arc = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=np.arctan(1/2), arc_center=origin_point, color=color_3)
        angle_label = Text("θ", color=color_3, font_size=20)
        angle_label.move_to(origin_point + RIGHT * 0.7 + UP * 0.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color_1))
        self.play(Create(x_axis), Create(y_axis), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_2)
        )
        self.play(Write(re_label), Write(im_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_3)
        )
        
        moving_dot = Dot(origin_point, color=color_3, radius=0.05)
        self.add(moving_dot)
        
        self.play(
            moving_dot.animate.move_to(point_coords),
            Create(vector_line),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(point_dot), Write(point_label))
        self.play(Create(angle_arc), Write(angle_label), Write(radius_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # Reset colors for final look
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title - Text mobject does not require LaTeX
        title = Text("The Secret of Imaginary Exponents", font_size=36)
        title.to_edge(UP)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)

        # 2. Create Complex Plane
        # Using label_constructor=Text avoids the default MathTex (which requires LaTeX)
        # We use NumberPlane instead of ComplexPlane to avoid the default "i" unit labels that force LaTeX
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": BLUE_D,
                "stroke_width": 1,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.3
            }
        ).add_coordinates(label_constructor=Text)
        
        self.play(Create(plane))

        # 3. Define Formula and Tracker
        # Using Text with unicode characters to avoid LaTeX requirement
        theta_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        formula = Text(
            "e^iθ = cos(θ) + i sin(θ)",
            color=WHITE,
            font_size=24
        ).to_corner(UL, buff=0.5).shift(DOWN * 0.7)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))

        # 4. Helper for point calculation - Fix: NumberPlane uses coords_to_point (or c2p)
        def get_complex_point():
            val = theta_tracker.get_value()
            return plane.coords_to_point(np.cos(val), np.sin(val))

        # 5. Redrawable Components
        vector = always_redraw(
            lambda: Vector(
                get_complex_point(),
                color=YELLOW
            )
        )
        
        unit_circle = Circle(
            radius=plane.get_x_unit_size(), 
            color=WHITE, 
            stroke_opacity=0.3
        )
        
        cos_line = always_redraw(
            lambda: Line(
                plane.coords_to_point(0, 0),
                plane.coords_to_point(np.cos(theta_tracker.get_value()), 0),
                color=BLUE,
                stroke_width=6
            )
        )
        
        sin_line = always_redraw(
            lambda: Line(
                plane.coords_to_point(np.cos(theta_tracker.get_value()), 0),
                get_complex_point(),
                color=RED,
                stroke_width=6
            )
        )

        cos_label = always_redraw(
            lambda: Text("cos(θ)", color=BLUE, font_size=18)
            .next_to(cos_line, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        )
        
        sin_label = always_redraw(
            lambda: Text("i sin(θ)", color=RED, font_size=18)
            .next_to(sin_line, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        )

        theta_arc = always_redraw(
            lambda: Arc(
                radius=0.4,
                start_angle=0,
                angle=theta_tracker.get_value(),
                color=YELLOW
            )
        )
        
        theta_symbol = always_redraw(
            lambda: Text("θ", color=YELLOW, font_size=18)
            .move_to(
                Arc(
                    radius=0.6,
                    start_angle=0,
                    angle=theta_tracker.get_value() if theta_tracker.get_value() > 0 else 0.001
                ).point_from_proportion(0.5)
            )
        )

        # 6. Execute Animations
        self.play(Create(unit_circle))
        self.play(Create(vector))
        self.play(
            Create(cos_line), 
            Create(sin_line), 
            FadeIn(cos_label), 
            FadeIn(sin_label)
        )
        self.play(Create(theta_arc), Write(theta_symbol))
        self.wait(1)

        # Rotation to PI/3
        self.play(theta_tracker.animate.set_value(PI/3), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # Full Rotation to 2*PI
        self.play(
            theta_tracker.animate.set_value(2*PI),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        # Reset and conclude
        self.play(theta_tracker.animate.set_value(0), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(2)

sections.example: Imagine five famous celebrities from different eras (Algebra, Geometry, Calculus) meeting at a single party hosted by Leonhard Euler.

sections.title: Prerequisite 1: The Nature of 'e' and 'i'
sections.content: Briefly define 'e' as the base of natural growth (scaling) and 'i' as the imaginary unit defined by i² = -1. Crucially, introduce the concept that multiplying by 'i' represents a 90-degree rotation on the complex plane rather than just a number.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Growth Seed' (e) that pushes numbers outward, and a 'Pivot Point' (i) that turns numbers like a steering wheel.

sections.title: Prerequisite 2: The Complex Plane
sections.content: Introduce the 2D coordinate system where the X-axis represents Real numbers and the Y-axis represents Imaginary numbers. Explain that any point can be described by its distance from the origin and its angle.
sections.example: An 'Explorer Drone' navigating a map where moving east-west is real and moving north-south is imaginary.

sections.title: The Secret of Imaginary Exponents
sections.content: Explain that while real exponents (e^x) cause growth/stretching, imaginary exponents (e^iθ) cause rotation along the unit circle. This is the core of Euler's Formula: e^(iθ) = cos(θ) + i sin(θ).
sections.example: A 'Merry-Go-Round' where the 'i' tells the ride to spin instead of flying away from the center. The angle θ is how far you have rotated.

sections.title: The Journey of π: Reaching the Destination
sections.content: Apply the concept to e^(iπ). Since π radians is exactly 180 degrees (a half-circle), the rotation starts at 1 on the Real axis and swings around to the opposite side.
sections.example: An 'Ant' starting at position (1,0) on a circle. It walks a distance of π (half the circumference) and ends up exactly at (-1,0).

sections.title: Conclusion: Synthesis and Impact
sections.content: Summarize the result: e^(iπ) = -1. Explain its significance in engineering and physics, specifically in representing waves, signals, and quantum mechanics through circular motion.
sections.example: Show a 'Radio Wave' oscillating, demonstrating how the rotation in the complex plane creates the smooth up-and-down motion of the signal.

storyboard.title: The Grand Reunion: Introduction to the Identity
lecture_lines: Behold the most beautiful equation in all of mathematics.
It unites five fundamental constants in a single identity.
Meet zero, one, e, i, and pi.
Geometry, calculus, and algebra converge in this expression.
Let's explore how these different worlds become one.
animations: Fade in the equation e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0 in white (#FFFFFF) at the center.
Highlight '0' and '1' with a blue (#0000FF) scale-up pulse.
Highlight '\pi' with a green (#00FF00) scale-up pulse.
Highlight 'e' and 'i' with a yellow (#FFFF00) scale-up pulse.
The entire equation glows and then fades out.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite 1: The Nature of 'e' and 'i'
lecture_lines: e is the fundamental base of natural growth.
i is defined as the square root of negative one.
Multiplying by i rotates a number by ninety degrees.
animations: Display 'e' (#00FF00) and a vector growing along the x-axis.
Display 'i' (#0000FF) and rotate the vector 90 degrees counter-clockwise.
Show the text "i^2 = -1" as the vector rotates another 90 degrees.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite 2: The Complex Plane
lecture_lines: The complex plane maps numbers in two dimensions.
Real numbers go horizontal; imaginary numbers go vertical.
Every point has a distance and a rotation angle.
animations: Draw [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/the.svg] Real axis (#FFFFFF) and Imaginary axis (#FFFF00) with labels.
Plot point (2, 1) and label it "2 + i".
Move a small dot from (0,0) to (2,1) following [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/the.svg] vector.

storyboard.title: The Secret of Imaginary Exponents
lecture_lines: Real exponents scale a value up or down.
Imaginary exponents do something different: they rotate.
The expression e to the i theta traces a circle.
Here, theta represents the angle of rotation.
Growth is transformed into continuous circular motion.
animations: Draw a grey unit circle (#555555) on the complex plane.
Display e^{i\theta} = \cos\theta + i\sin\theta (#FFFFFF) above the circle.
Animate a vector rotating from angle 0 to \theta.
Project a vertical line to the x-axis, labeled \cos\theta.
Project a horizontal line to the y-axis, labeled i\sin\theta.

storyboard.title: The Journey of π: Reaching the Destination
lecture_lines: Set the rotation angle to exactly pi radians.
Pi radians corresponds to a perfect half-circle.
We start at positive one on the real axis.
A half-circle rotation lands us at negative one.
Therefore, e to the power i pi is negative one.
animations: Start with a unit circle and vector at point (1, 0).
Rotate the vector 180 degrees counter-clockwise to point (-1, 0).
Display the identity e^{i\pi} = -1 (#FFFFFF) near the vector tip.
Transform the identity into e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0 by moving terms.
Draw a glowing gold box (#FFD700) around the final formula.

storyboard.title: Conclusion: Synthesis and Impact
lecture_lines: This identity links exponential growth to circular rotation.
It underpins modern physics, signal processing, and waves.
Complexity simplifies into this one elegant truth.
animations: Synchronize the rotation of the vector with a traveling sine wave.
Display floating labels "Signal Processing" and "Quantum Waves" (#00FFFF).
Fade everything to leave e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0 in the center.
